Each task declares one tuning number. In XP mode it is the base experience per action, which * the current tier multiplies; a rough guide is that Dragon arrives at * {@code 273742 / (rate * 1.5)} actions. In LINEAR mode it is the number of actions that reaches * 99, used for bounded collections. * *

The past participle and unit either side of the description build the count sentence: "spun * the camera" plus "time" reads as "You have spun the camera 10 times." The participle matters, * so "run out of energy" rather than "ran out of energy". Keep the copy plain; the names carry * the joke and the lines underneath should not try to. */ public final class TaskRegistry { public static final ImmutableList TASKS = ImmutableList.of( // Rate 1, the floor, because this is the loosest trigger in the registry: every menu click // counts, including walking. Named for the wider thing // rather than filtered down to eating, which would throw away half of what it sees. unique("gourmet", "Gourmet", "Consume a unique item.", "consumed", "different thing", "You have never consumed anything.", 300, TaskEventType.CONSUMED, null), unique("wardrobe", "Wardrobe", "Equip a unique item.", "worn", "different item", "You have never worn anything.", 1000, TaskEventType.ITEM_ACTION, e -> "wear".equals(e.getText()) || "wield".equals(e.getText())), unique("transmuter", "Transmuter", "Alch a unique item.", "alched", "different item", "You have never alched anything.", 500, TaskEventType.ALCH, null), unique("antiquarian", "Antiquarian", "Examine a unique object.", "examined", "different object", "You have never examined any scenery.", 3000, TaskEventType.OBJECT_ACTION, e -> e.getText().startsWith("examine|")) ); private static Task xp(String id, String name, String description, String verb, String unit, String never, int rate, TaskEventType trigger, Predicate filter) { return new Task(id, name, description, verb, unit, never, Task.Mode.XP, rate, false, false, true, trigger, filter); } /** * A task that counts every event, with no one per tick cap. * *

Two things qualify. Either the clicking itself is the subject, where capping the rate * would measure the wrong thing entirely, or the game already decides how often the event can * happen, where a cap is a no op that only looks like a safeguard. The second kind is why this * is stated rather than left to coincidence: a task counting a server side success message is * safe today because that message cannot arrive twice in a tick, which is a fact about the * game rather than anything this code enforces. */ private static Task xpEvery(String id, String name, String description, String verb, String unit, String never, int rate, TaskEventType trigger, Predicate filter) { return new Task(id, name, description, verb, unit, never, Task.Mode.XP, rate, false, false, false, trigger, filter); } /** For counters measured in the event value rather than in events. */ private static Task xpWeighted(String id, String name, String description, String verb, String unit, String never, int rate, TaskEventType trigger, Predicate filter) { return new Task(id, name, description, verb, unit, never, Task.Mode.XP, rate, false, true, true, trigger, filter); } private static final ImmutableMap BY_ID; static { ImmutableMap.Builder builder = ImmutableMap.builder(); for (Task task : TASKS) { builder.put(task.getId(), task); } BY_ID = builder.build(); } /** Lookup for stats that mirror a task rather than keeping their own counter. */ static Task byId(String id) { return BY_ID.get(id); } /** Bounded collections: linear levelling against a known pool size, counting distinct ids. */ private static Task unique(String id, String name, String description, String verb, String unit, String never, int target, TaskEventType trigger, Predicate filter) { // Unique tasks need no cap: a repeated value is already rejected as one it has seen. return new Task(id, name, description, verb, unit, never, Task.Mode.LINEAR, target, true, false, false, trigger, filter); } /** * Scenery matching. OBJECT_ACTION carries "option|name" because doors, gates, ladders and * staircases are indistinguishable by their menu option alone. */ private static boolean objectAction(TaskEvent event, String option, String nameFragment) { String text = event.getText(); int split = text.indexOf('|'); return split > 0 && text.startsWith(option) && text.substring(split + 1).contains(nameFragment); } /** * A log actually handed over, "You get some yew logs." and its many variants. * *

Matched on the shape rather than on a list of tree types, which would need editing every * time one is added. Bark and bruma roots use the same opening and are correctly left out, * because neither of them is a log. */ private static boolean isLogObtained(TaskEvent event) { String msg = event.getText(); return msg.startsWith("you get ") && msg.contains("log"); } /** * A failed pickpocket, and not a failed lockpick. * *

"You fail to pick the lock." shares its opening with "You fail to pick the guard's * pocket.", so matching the opening alone had this counting picked locks as being caught, * which is neither what the task says nor embarrassing. */ private static boolean isFailedPickpocket(TaskEvent event) { String msg = event.getText(); return msg.startsWith("you fail to pick ") && msg.contains("pocket"); } /** A successful pickpocket. "You pick the lock." shares the opening and is not one. */ static boolean isPickpocket(TaskEvent event) { String msg = event.getText(); return msg.startsWith("you pick ") && msg.contains("pocket"); } /** * Only the message for actually applying compost. Inspecting a treated patch says "has been * treated with compost" and "has already been treated with compost", neither of which is an * action the player just took. */ private static boolean isCompostApplied(TaskEvent event) { String msg = event.getText(); return msg.contains("you treat the") && msg.contains("compost"); } /** Matches the two server messages for swinging at a tree without a usable axe. */ private static boolean isAxeComplaint(TaskEvent event) { String msg = event.getText(); return msg.contains("need an axe") || msg.contains("do not have an axe"); } /** The game has several ways of saying the same thing about a stuffed inventory. */ private static boolean isInventoryFull(TaskEvent event) { String msg = event.getText(); return msg.contains("not enough space") || msg.contains("inventory is too full") || msg.contains("enough inventory space") || msg.contains("hands are full"); } private static boolean isAgilityFail(TaskEvent event) { String msg = event.getText(); return msg.contains("you slip and fall") || msg.contains("lose your footing") || msg.contains("miss the ledge"); } private TaskRegistry() { } }
